question: Should Twilio RCS become a bundled OpenClaw channel, remain an installable external plugin, or be split so only generic webhook hardening lands in core?
rationale: The code can use existing plugin seams, but bundling creates a permanent service-specific support and configuration commitment that automation cannot authorize.

options.title: External plugin first
options.body: Keep the RCS implementation outside bundled core and publish it through the supported plugin ecosystem after live proof and package cleanup.

options.title: Sponsor bundled RCS
options.body: Accept RCS as a bundled channel after the contributor supplies live Twilio proof and maintainers regenerate or explicitly authorize the dependency graph.

options.title: Split generic hardening
options.body: Extract the core HTTP-route registration and SMS collision behavior into a narrow reviewed change while keeping the RCS channel external.

recommendation.title: External plugin first
recommendation.body: Keep the RCS implementation outside bundled core and publish it through the supported plugin ecosystem after live proof and package cleanup.

likelyOwner.reason: The most direct merged feature-history signal is the bundled Twilio SMS channel architecture that establishes the adjacent product tier and ownership precedent.
